In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TIMP‐1 is a useful marker for the assessment of disease activity of AD, especially for the chronicity of AD, while MMP‐3 does not seem to be a useful marker for AD.
the increased levels of serum TIM-1 in AD may reflect the severity of chronic lesions, and that the serum TIMP-1 may be a useful indicator of the long-term disease activity of AD.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the serum levels of tissue inhibitors of metallopeptidases (TIMP)‐1 but not MMP‐3 are significantly elevated in patients with atopic dermatitis, which may be useful for the evaluation of long‐term activity of this disease.
the elevated levels of TIMP-1 may be a useful indicator of the severity of AD and may be involved in the pathogenesis, especially the chronic lesions of AD.
TIMP‐1 may contribute to the chronicity of AD by inhibiting the proteolytic activity of MMPs.

serum TIMP‐3 is elevated in patients with AD.

the TIMP-1/MMP-3 ratio is a useful marker for the evaluation of the disease status in AD patients, and that the TIMP‐1 may be a useful serum marker for the long‐term evaluation of disease activity in AD.
